An action item is created and later in the same meeting explicitly removed or cancelled. The action item has status dropped. Record an F3 fact of type action_item_removed linked to it.

argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0303c: meeting "c" (conceptual design) of series SY0303.

PROJECT
The team is designing a children's educational tablet case.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Marketing Expert (ME)  Priya  present
B  User Interface designer (UI)  Tom  present
C  Industrial Designer (ID)  Lena  present
D  Project Manager (PM)  Marcus  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0303a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, noted that the marketing expert was absent for the day, and had the user interface designer and industrial designer introduce themselves. He presented the project, a protective case for the company's existing children's educational tablet, to be sold separately as an accessory and sold internationally, and led a whiteboard warm-up in which each member drew a favourite animal. He gave the financial targets: a selling price of 25 euros and a maximum unit production cost of 12.50 euros, excluding packaging. The team discussed initial ideas, including the need to survive frequent drops and a carrying handle that could fold into a stand, and agreed on a target age group of four to eight. The industrial designer declared EVA foam as the material, but nobody agreed and the project manager deferred the material question. He then assigned preparation tasks, including market research for the absent marketing expert.
  decisions: The target age group for the case is children aged four to eight.
  actions: The industrial designer will research the working design, including materials and drop protection. The user interface designer will study how children interact with the case, including the handle, stand, access to buttons and charging port, and the screen protector. The marketing expert, who was absent, will do market research on what parents want in a case and on competitors' products and prices. The project manager will email the brief and her task to the marketing expert. The project manager will send out the minutes of the meeting. The project manager will check with management whether there is a required company colour scheme.
  problems: The case material is unresolved. EVA foam was put forward but not agreed, and the decision was postponed until costs are known. The 12.50 euro production cost limit is considered tight for a durable children's case. It is unknown whether the case must follow a company colour scheme or look. The marketing expert has not yet been informed of her assignment.
  action item SY0303a.ai1: Research the working design of the case, including materials and drop protection, for the next meeting. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0303a.ai2: Study how children interact with the case (handle, stand, access to buttons and charging port), including the screen protector. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0303a.ai3: Do market research on what parents look for in a tablet case and on competitors' cases and prices. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0303a.ai4: Email the project brief and her market research task to the absent marketing expert. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0303a.ai5: Send out the minutes of the kickoff meeting. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0303a.ai6: Check with management whether the case must follow a company colour scheme or look. (owner D, active)
  fact (absence): Priya (A), the marketing expert, was absent from the kickoff meeting, reportedly at a trade show all day.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): Lena (C) declared that the case would be made of EVA foam and called it decided, but nobody agreed. Tom (B) hesitated and Marcus (D) postponed the material question until costs are known.

[SY0303b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting, noted that the industrial designer was absent through illness, and welcomed the marketing expert, who had missed the kickoff and confirmed she had received the brief and minutes. He recapped the kickoff: the target age group of four to eight was agreed, while the material was still open after the industrial designer's EVA foam proposal. He reported that management requires the company logo and the company yellow on the case. The marketing expert presented her market research. Competitor cases sell for roughly 15 to 30 euros. Parents rank drop protection first, ease of cleaning second and a carrying handle third, and only one competitor case offered a stand. The user interface designer presented how children use the tablet. He recommended thick, grippy edges, soft covers over the volume buttons, a slightly recessed power button and an open charging port. He also proposed a raised lip around the screen instead of a separate screen protector. The team agreed on the raised lip and confirmed the handle that folds into a stand. The material question was handed to the absent industrial designer for costing. A parent survey was assigned to the marketing expert and then cancelled within the meeting.
  decisions: The case will have a raised lip around the screen, and no separate screen protector will be included. The handle that folds into a stand will be kept as a key feature and selling point. The planned parent survey through the company newsletter was cancelled, and the team will rely on the marketing expert's existing research.
  actions: The industrial designer, who was absent, will cost EVA foam against silicone relative to the 12.50 euro limit, check whether foam can be wiped clean, and send the figures before the next meeting. The project manager assigned this task. The project manager will email the industrial designer her task and the minutes today. The marketing expert will look into colour trends for children's products that work with the company yellow. The user interface designer will sketch the button cut-outs and the handle-stand for the conceptual design meeting. The project manager will send out the minutes.
  problems: The case material, EVA foam or silicone, is still unresolved and waits for the industrial designer's cost figures. The 12.50 euro production cost limit remains tight, especially if silicone is used. A shoulder strap was suggested but parked over safety concerns for young children. The raised lip protects against drops but not against scratches.
  action item SY0303b.ai1: Cost EVA foam against silicone relative to the 12.50 euro production limit, check whether foam can be wiped clean, and send figures before the next meeting. (owner C, active)
  action item SY0303b.ai2: Email the absent industrial designer her costing task and the minutes today. (owner D, active)
  action item SY0303b.ai3: Run a quick parent survey through the company newsletter on the strap, the handle and willingness to pay. (owner A, dropped)
  action item SY0303b.ai4: Look into colour trends for children's products that work with the company yellow. (owner A, active)
  action item SY0303b.ai5: Sketch the button cut-outs and the handle-stand for the conceptual design meeting. (owner B, active)
  action item SY0303b.ai6: Send out the minutes of the meeting. (owner D, active)
  fact (absence): Lena (C), the industrial designer, was absent from the functional design meeting because she was off sick.
  fact (action_item_removed): The parent survey was cancelled later in the meeting because the newsletter goes out only at the end of the month, too late for results.
  fact (plan_change): The kickoff idea of including a screen protector was replaced by a raised lip, because children peel protectors off.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): Priya (A) suggested a shoulder strap. Tom (B) raised safety concerns and it was parked, not agreed.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F3_UNAGREED_DECISION [F3]: Someone raises a proposal as if it were a decision, but no one agrees to it and the meeting moves on without settling it. Record an F3 fact of type unagreed_proposal with agreed false. It must not appear in summary.decisions.
  Required gold labels: summary, qa_facts, edge_cases.
- F3_ACTION_REMOVED [F3]: An action item is created and later in the same meeting explicitly removed or cancelled. The action item has status dropped. Record an F3 fact of type action_item_removed linked to it.
  Required gold labels: action_items, qa_facts, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
